subject: Proposal: Transfer Addendum approach for Acme Insights — SCCs routing & processor obligations
messages:
From: Nina Park <legal@acmeinsights.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmeinsights.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Draft transfer addendum + SCCs approach for Redwood (Acme Insights)

Marissa / Ben —

Thanks again for the discussion yesterday. Attached is our latest redline to the DPA (Acme_DPA_Redline_v3.docx) and a short note from procurement on signing cadence. High level asks from Acme Legal: we need clarity on (1) cross-border routing for model inference, (2) processor vs controller roles for subcomponents (logging/analytics), and (3) a fall-back approach if SCCs become unavailable (route to EU-only hosting / transfer addendum).

We'd prefer a single transfer addendum that:
- documents the chosen SCCs clause set,
- lists subprocessors and their regions, and
- includes a short mitigation appendix for “SCCs unavailable” scenarios (e.g., onshore-only option + KMS key residency).

Can Redwood confirm if the proposed redline (track changes) is implementable operationally? In particular, our security team flagged the KV cache described in section 3.2 — does that introduce any additional export controls we should call out?

Proposed next steps: quick call with legal + security this week, then procurement to push DocuSign. We have a constrained board approval window and would like to close order form by 01/31.

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Redline_v3.docx (Word doc, 32 KB)

—
Nina Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Acme Insights
legal@acmeinsights.com
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Nina Park <legal@acmeinsights.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 08:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft transfer addendum + SCCs approach for Redwood (Acme Insights)

Nina — thanks, received and reviewed the redline at a high level. I looped in Ben (contracts) and Laura (privacy) to confirm legal and operational feasibility. Quick thoughts before we sync:

1) SCCs / routing: we can support SCCs and provide an explicit routing policy that pins inference to EU regions for EU-scoped data. That routing policy can be surfaced in the transfer addendum as an operational control (we'll include the precise region list).

2) KV cache / export controls: our runtime stores transient KV cache for in-flight sessions. It is not persisted long-term and is encrypted in transit + at rest. That said, if Acme needs a stronger residency guarantee we can add an included mitigation: ephemeral cache eviction on session close + EU-only KMS for keys associated with EU traffic.

3) Roles: we agree to a split where Redwood is the processor; Acme remains controller. For analytics/logging, we propose an exhibit that lists telemetry types we collect and a processors sub-list (e.g., Datadog-us-east will not process EU-scoped PII).

Ben / Laura — can you review the attached and call out redlines we should push back on? If we accept the ‘SCCs-unavailable’ fallback language, we need a clear technical fallback path (EU-only routing + optional dedicated instance) and an associated SOW/price impact line for Dedicated capacity.

I can do a 30-min align tomorrow 10–10:30 PT. Nina / procurement — does that work?

Attachment: Redwood_Transfer_Addendum_Draft.pdf (PDF, 18 KB)

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Draft transfer addendum + SCCs approach for Redwood (Acme Insights)

Marissa / Laura —

Thanks for the ping. I scanned Acme's redline and have inline comments in the attached copy (see 'Acme_DPA_Redline_v3.docx' with our edits). Summary of our positions:

- We accept controller/processor split and will sign SCCs so long as the addendum narrows responsibilities for subcomponents (we won't agree to broad controller-like obligations for open telemetry).
- For the KV cache callout: operationally we can do ephemeral-only caching for Acme EU traffic. If Acme requires guaranteed zero-export for session keys, propose a short addendum clause and pricing for Dedicated EU-only instance (estimate: +20% on order form).
- SCCs-unavailable fallback: we can provide the fallback but must include a clear SLA and rollback timeline (e.g., Redwood will either enable EU routing within 7 business days or provide temporary Dedicated capacity for up to 30 days).

I also flagged a compliance checkbox: if Acme expects monthly audit access to logs for EU traffic, we need a scoping note (how logs are redacted, retention). That can go into Exhibit B.

Recommend:
- Push the fallback language to include two options (EU routing or Dedicated).
- Add a short pricing note in the order form that enumerates the cost impact of Dedicated capacity for EU-only routing.

I can be on the sync tomorrow and will bring the compliance runbook.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Nina Park <legal@acmeinsights.com>, procurement@acmeinsights.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Draft transfer addendum + SCCs approach for Redwood (Acme Insights)

Nina — thanks for the quick turnaround. Following internal review, here's a consolidated proposal we can present to Acme Legal / Procurement: 

Mutual proposal (summary):
- Execute Acme_DPA_Redline_v3 with Redwood's inline edits (attached).
- Transfer addendum will explicitly enumerate permitted SCCs and include an operational routing appendix (EU regions + IP ranges reference).
- KV cache: Redwood will enable ephemeral-only cache for EU-scoped traffic; for guaranteed residency we offer a Dedicated EU-only deployment as an optional add-on (price impact to be shown on order form).
- SCCs-unavailable fallback: Redwood will provide either (a) EU routing change within 7 business days, or (b) temporary Dedicated capacity for up to 30 days while long-term solution is implemented. We will include rollback timing and SLAs in Exhibit C.
- Audit & logs: monthly scoped audit access per Exhibit B with redaction rules; retention configurable per order form.

Next steps / mutual action plan:
1) Acme Legal to confirm whether the two-option fallback is acceptable (EU routing OR Dedicated).
2) Redwood to push our inline redlines to the DocuSign packet and provide pricing addendum for Dedicated option. (Target: order form update by 01/18).
3) Small legal + security sync (30 min) to finalize Exhibit B redaction rules — proposed slot: Mon 15 Jan 10:00–10:30 PT.
4) Procurement to authorize DocuSign send once legal signs off.

I will attach the edited redline and the transfer addendum draft to the DocuSign packet. If that aligns with Acme's timeline, we think 01/31 is an achievable close.

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Redline_v3.docx (with Redwood inline edits), Redwood_Transfer_Addendum_Draft.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123
